title: Tenant-aware surge decompression and backpressure signal tuning
creator: Avery Chen
description: Follow-up for the Feb 26 hosted API GPU capacity exhaustion incident (INC-2026-02-26). Goal: implement a tenant-aware surge decompression strategy and refine the backpressure signals so that multi-tenant request storms don't create persistent queue amplification and large-scale throttling. This ticket captures the investigation summary, proposed design, and concrete action items across runtime, autoscaler, and console teams.
comments: 2026-02-27 - Avery Chen: Triage meeting notes — incident root-cause hypothesis: simultaneous high-concurrency long-context workloads from 3 tenants caused GPU pool occupancy to increase; KV cache churn and longer per-token compute meant requests held GPUs longer than expected. Autoscaler hysteresis and 90s evaluation window delayed capacity reaction; admission logic treats all tenants equally so a single noisy tenant amplified queue growth.

2026-03-01 - Miguel Torres: Investigation updates — reproduced load pattern in staging using bench harness (bench/storm-runner v2). Observed p99 queue latency correlates with pool utilization > 82% and with increase in average tokens generated per request. Found admission scoring doesn't account for expected remaining tokens; requests that expand (chat continuations) can occupy GPU for multiple seconds after admission — we should add an estimated remaining-cost field to scoring.

2026-03-02 - Priya Menon (SRE): Grafana snapshots uploaded to postmortem: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted/gpu-capacity?panelId=7 — shows queue growth, per-tenant QPS, and autoscaler scale events lag. Also recorded GPU scheduler traces at /s3/incident/2026-02-26/traces.tgz.

2026-03-03 - Miguel Torres: Design proposal posted: Confluence -> https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-247531 — key ideas: (1) tenant soft-queue caps (per-pool) with proportional fairness; (2) early spillback signal computed from p95 queue latency + estimated remaining-cost; (3) staggered decompression: when draining backlog, release requests in controlled batches (burst windows) to avoid re-amplifying occupancy; (4) reduce autoscaler evaluation window from 90s -> 30s for hosted pools and add predictive prewarm trigger when sustained enqueue rate > threshold.

2026-03-05 - Design review (feedback from Console team): Add a visualization in Console showing per-tenant queue pressure and current soft-cap vs hard-cap. Also surface spillback reason codes so customers can see if they were intentionally spilled back due to fairness or capacity.

2026-03-06 - Miguel Torres: Implementation plan — split work across three PRs: runtime (spillback signal + tenant caps), autoscaler (window tuning + prewarm hook), console (dashboard + disclosures). Owners assigned: runtime -> Miguel, autoscaler -> Li Wei, console -> Sandra Park. Target alpha deploy to staging 2026-03-12.

2026-03-08 - Runtime patch PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 — changes: (a) expose estimated_remaining_tokens in admission payload, (b) compute tenant_backpressure_score = p95_queue_latency_ms * (1 + estimated_remaining_tokens/avg_tokens), (c) if score > threshold, tag request with spillback=true and reason=TENANT_FAIR_CAP. Tests: unit + load test added (bench/storm-runner config).

2026-03-09 - Autoscaler PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/4832 — changes: (a) eval window reduced to 30s for hosted GPU pools, (b) new prewarm trigger: if sustained enqueue_rate > 2x baseline for 20s, start warm-up (spin up 1 primed instance), (c) safety cap added to avoid oscillation: backoff multiplier and minimum hold time 45s.

2026-03-10 - SRE note: Runbook update proposed — add a step to inspect per-tenant queue charts and to perform emergency tenant throttles (rate-limits) when spike is traced to single customer. Also added a checklist for staged decompression during manual intervention.

2026-03-10 - Miguel Torres: Current status — runtime PR merged to canary branch, autoscaler PR under review, console dashboard mockups ready. Next: stage-wide canary deploy to us-west-2 pools on 2026-03-12, run targeted chaos test where one tenant issues a synthetic long-context surge to validate spillback and decompression behavior.
notes: Accepted trade-offs: we prioritize tail-latency protection and fairness over raw aggregate throughput during tenant storms — this will temporarily increase overall token cost but prevents broad customer-visible throttling.

Follow-ups (post-deploy): (1) run A/B comparing 30s vs 15s autoscaler window to quantify cost/latency tradeoff, (2) instrument per-tenant estimated_remaining_tokens accuracy and iterate estimator, (3) consider quota-based hard caps for repeat offenders.
Postmortem link (final) will be attached after the canary validation run and customer-impact reconciliation.
